title: Creditless burst fabric & soft fence — design sketch
body:
Context and problem statement

We have a lot of prior work exploring credit pools, burst ledgers, and epochal quotas for Dedicated customers. Those systems work but add bookkeeping, billing edge cases, and can be surprising for customers when credits run out. This sketch proposes a different orbit: a creditless burst fabric + soft fence controls. The goal is to enable short-term burst behavior (handle traffic spikes) while providing strong tenant isolation and predictable latency without per-tenant credit accounting.

High-level idea (TL;DR)

- Instead of explicit per-tenant burst credits, we build a dynamic, time-windowed resource fabric that rebalances capacity among tenants according to a latency budget and usage curvature.
- Soft fences are lightweight runtime constraints that temporarily limit a tenant’s affinity to hot nodes or preemption radius when they cross behavior thresholds. They do not evict or debit tokens; they probabilistically steer traffic and reduce headroom to protect SLOs for neighbors.
- Autoscaler integration: cluster-level autoscalers use a weighted smoothing function of steady-state commit + short-term burst demand signals to provision fast warm pools without doing per-tenant accounting.

Why this might be better

- Simpler billing/UX: customers don’t have to reason about credits and credit exhaustion.
- Smoother degradations: soft fences gracefully throttle noisy tenants rather than hard preemptions.
- Operational simplicity: avoids complex ledgers and expiry semantics.

Core concepts and components

1) Fabric window and budgeted latency
- Each physical pool (GPU rack/zone) maintains a sliding fabric window (e.g., 30s) capturing demand, latencies, inflight tokens, and KV cache hotness distribution per tenant (anonymized counts).
- The fabric computes per-tenant "latency budget pressure" = (p95 latency - target) * relative qps share, smoothed. Positive pressure indicates a tenant is consuming disproportionate low-latency resources.
- The fabric exposes a single numercial ledger-like score per tenant (pressure_score) used by routing and soft fences. This is ephemeral, rolling, and not billed.

2) Soft fence primitives
- SoftFence(mode, degree, ttl): Mode {affinity_reduction, prewarm_block, queue_limit}, degree 0..1, ttl seconds.
- Soft fences are issued when pressure_score crosses configurable thresholds. They are unidirectional hints to the routing/orchestrator and to local node decision logic.
- Example: affinity_reduction 0.6 means reduce placement locality for this tenant by 60% (i.e., spread the tenant across more nodes to avoid hot KV cache monopolization).

3) Creditless burst fabric behavior
- When a burst arrives, fabric looks at cluster-level headroom and p95 tails for other tenants, then calculates an allocation fraction per tenant proportional to (1 - pressure_score) * baseline_share, clipped to safe headroom.
- Allocate ephemeral fast-path slots (short lived, e.g., 10s buckets) which allow low-latency responses. These slots are not charged as credits but are subject to preemption/backoff.
- If capacity runs tight, fabric issues SoftFences to noisy tenants instead of hard evictions. Soft fences step down latency targets gracefully.

4) Autoscaler integration
- Two signals exported to cluster autoscaler: sustained_commit_rate and burst_pressure (fabric aggregated). Autoscaler uses a two-timescale policy: scale-to-commit for mid-long term (minutes), and maintain a warm pool target proportional to recent burst_pressure for fast reaction.
- Warm pool is distinct from reserved capacity. Warm pool nodes are kept in a partially primed state (models loaded, but throttled). They can be promoted to full serving in ~5–15s depending on model size and quantization state.

5) Routing and fallback policies
- Smart router consults fabric pressure_score and soft fences before pinning a request to fast-path. If request is ineligible for fast-path, router may: fall back to slower-optimized model variant, queue request with backoff, or route to a different region/tenant-reserved pool depending on customer config.
- Customer-facing control: allowlist of fallback modes per tenant (best-effort, reduced-fidelity, reserve-fallback).

6) Observability and user feedback
- Surface pressure_score and active soft fences in Console with timeline views and suggested mitigations.
- Provide simulated "burst replay" tool that shows how a given traffic trace would have been handled under current policy (for customers doing capacity planning).

SLOs and acceptance criteria

- For non-noisy tenants under normal load, p95 latency regression < 10% compared to baseline for 99% of 1-hour windows after rollout.
- For noisy tenants experiencing soft fencing, degrade gracefully: p95 may increase up to configured max_degradation (user-configurable, default 2x) but error rate should remain < 0.5% due to preemption.
- Warm pool promotion latency: median < 8s, p95 < 20s for quantized LLMs in target regions.
- Platform-level availability during bursts: no more than 0.1% of requests receive hard-fail (capacity rejection) due to breach for customers with reserved capacity.

Implementation sketch and runtime hooks

- Fabric controller: lightweight service running per-pool that ingests request telemetry, KV cache hit signals, and latency histograms (aggregated and anonymized). Must be highly available and read-mostly for routers.
- Router hook: consult fabric for pressure_score, accept soft fence hints, choose fast-path eligibility. Must be low-latency (<1ms added).
- Node runtime: honor soft fence decisions (e.g., reduce affinity, deprioritize KV cache warming for flagged tenant), expose local metrics.
- Autoscaler ext: new warm pool API and signals (burst_pressure).

Config surface and customer controls

- Per-customer: target_latency_profile, max_degradation, fallback_mode_prefs, warm_pool_priority (low/med/high), isolation_sensitivity (sensitive customers can opt into stronger soft fences or guaranteed fast-path windows).
- Admin: pool-level thresholds for pressure -> soft fence transition, global headroom target, warm pool sizing multiplier.

Rollout plan (phases)

1) Canary: implement fabric controller with read-only router integration and surface metrics. Run in passive mode in 1 us-west pool for 2 weeks.
2) Active canary: enable soft fence enforcement for 10% of traffic for low-risk tenants (internal + beta). Monitor SLOs, manual rollback ready.
3) Scoped rollout: expand to several pools and enable warm pool promotion API. Add Console UI.
4) General availability: enable for all Dedicated pools with opt-in flags for customers to select fallback modes.

Operational concerns and failure modes

- Fabric controller failure: routers fall back to baseline routing (no fast-path). Must fail open to avoid blackholing traffic.
- Bad fence oscillation: hysteresis and TTLs; implement exponential backoff on fence re-issuing to avoid flip-flop.
- Warm pool thrash: guard with admission control and warm-promote cooldowns.

Open questions / tradeoffs

- How much complexity are customers willing to accept in exchange for no credits? Some customers prefer explicit credit accounting for billing predictability. We may need an opt-in "visible credits" view for customers who want to reconcile behavior to cost.
- Telemetry privacy: fabric needs per-tenant hotness signals; ensure metrics are aggregated and PII-free and conform to audited telemetry policies.
- Billing alignment: if we remove credits, how to reconcile usage-based billing during bursts (should bursts increase billed tokens or be amortized?). Product input required.

Next steps (short term TODOs)

- Engineering: prototype fabric controller ingest and compute pressure_score; instrument one small pool. (@Julian)
- Runtime: add soft fence hook points in router and node runtime to accept hints; minimal semantics only. (@Ruth)
- Product: define fallback_mode options & billing implications; draft Console UX copy. (@Ivan)
- SRE: run chaos tests for fence TTL oscillation scenarios. (@Samir)

Notes to reviewers

- This is a high-level sketch exploring a creditless path. I'm intentionally leaving some gaps (billing, exact math) to solicit product and finance input. The core hypothesis: you can get better customer experience and simpler ops by avoiding an explicit burst-credit ledger and using ephemeral pressure-based steering and soft fences.

- Please call out any regulatory or billing constraints that would force us to keep explicit per-tenant accounting. Also flag any SLO or telemetry privacy concerns.

References and related drafts

- See related folder notes: several prior PRDs on credit pools and burst ledgers (we should reconcile and map concepts).
- Prototype telemetry collector: DED-908.

-- end of sketch --
